title: Direct vs Regular Mutual Funds: Understanding SEBI's New Default Rule
description: Regular mutual funds include a commission for distributors, leading to higher expense ratios. Direct mutual funds do not include distributor commissions, resu.

faq.q: What is the main benefit of a Direct Plan mutual fund?
faq.a: The primary benefit is a lower Total Expense Ratio (TER) because it does not include distributor commissions. This means more of your investment compounds, leading to potentially higher returns over the long term.

faq.q: Can I switch my existing Regular Plan investments to Direct Plans?
faq.a: Yes, you can. The process typically involves redeeming your units from the Regular Plan and then reinvesting the proceeds into the corresponding Direct Plan of the same fund. Be aware of potential exit loads and capital gains tax implications.

faq.q: Does investing in a Direct Plan mean I don't get any advice?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Direct Plans mean you are not paying for advice through the fund's expense ratio. You can still seek advice from a fee-only Certified Financial Planner (CFP) and then execute your investments directly.

faq.q: How do I find Direct Plans for mutual funds?
faq.a: You can find Direct Plans on the respective Asset Management Company's (AMC) website, through platforms like MF Utility (MFU), or through specific online platforms that specialise in direct mutual funds.

faq.q: What is SEBI's role in this new default rule?
faq.a: SEBI, as the market regulator, introduced this rule to ensure transparency and protect investor interests. By making Direct Plans the default for execution-only platforms, SEBI aims to reduce investment costs for investors and improve their net returns.

faq.q: Are Direct Plans suitable for all investors?
faq.a: Direct Plans are generally suitable for investors who are comfortable making their own investment decisions or who seek advice from a fee-only advisor and prefer to execute transactions independently to save on costs.

faq.q: Will this rule impact my investments through an advisor?
faq.a: If your advisor is registered and provides advisory services, they will likely continue to recommend Regular Plans (where they earn commission) or charge you a direct fee for their services. The new rule primarily impacts execution-only platforms.
